target: Finalize, package, publish, transactionally install, and verify the completed R1-R8 modularization without adding Summary V2 or changing persisted behavior.
primary_semantics: 2.19.0 is the first public integration release of the completed R1-R8 ownership refactor; the release must preserve all 2.15.0 user-visible and persisted contracts while installing the exact evaluated candidate.
invariants: Raw archives, completed summaries, indexes, cloud envelopes, cursors, device identities, and active archive content are not modified by release finalization or installation.
The active archive-root pointer is preserved byte-for-byte across a successful upgrade and restored after any failed upgrade.
Only one collector startup owner is active after installation, and its running binary belongs to the installed 2.19.0 generation.
The Windows dashboard shortcut targets the packaged native launcher, uses the packaged icon, contains no command-line arguments, and never retains an obsolete Python path.
Windows installer processes used by routine activation remain hidden and do not steal foreground focus.
Cloud configuration, peer trust, Environment state, summary backlog, and maintenance queues retain their pre-install meaning and are not reset or claimed complete.
R1-R8 canonical owners and independent failure domains remain intact.
A passing test, file, process, tag, or installer alone never proves active runtime success; the real entrypoint and promised state transition must be observed.
Any failed case is repaired at the narrowest existing canonical owner after checking the complete shared invariant set; no additive bypass may mask the failure.
A repair cannot regress an earlier passing case that shares the changed owner, persisted state, scheduler, installer, launcher, or release contract.
allowed_changes: Change the declared product and native binary versions from 2.18.0 to 2.19.0.
Add the 2.19.0 release contract, release-contract tests, governance receipts, rehearsal evidence, independent evaluation, promotion review, and release notes.
Update all three README files and the documentation contract for the same release semantics.
Correct an existing canonical release or installation owner only when a frozen rehearsal exposes a confirmed blocker and the repair is smaller than adding a competing path.
prohibited_changes: Add, integrate, alter, or claim Summary V2 rescue or atomic summary behavior.
Change archive, summary, index, Environment, attachment, evidence, federation, cloud, update-signature, or collector event formats.
Introduce a new installer, updater, scheduler, dashboard launcher, archive pointer, rollback journal, or background owner alongside the canonical implementation.
Add speculative fallback behavior, compatibility shims without a proven caller, duplicate wrappers, new dependencies, or broad abstractions solely to make a failed case pass.
Publish or install a candidate whose bytes differ from the independently evaluated artifact.
Delete or replace the previous installed generation before the new generation has passed the transactional installed-effect probe.
Claim macOS real-device installation from Windows or from package construction alone.
before_after_checks: Compare the complete public CLI and documentation contracts before and after the version-only release delta.
Compare the active archive-root pointer, configuration, device identity, cloud configuration, queue counts, and archive authority hashes before and after isolated and real installation.

Exercise clean Windows installation, 2.15.0-to-2.19.0 upgrade, interrupted upgrade rollback, collector generation handoff, shortcut recreation, and no-focus-steal behavior through production entrypoints.
Build and inspect Windows x64 and macOS universal installers from the exact candidate; verify packaged files, binary versions, hashes, and signed update metadata.
Run the full Python suite, all Rust targets, architecture contract, documentation contract, and complete release rehearsal against one frozen source-content hash.
After any repair, rerun the failed case plus all cases sharing the changed Owner or invariant, then freeze a new candidate hash before evaluation.

original_triggers: The completed R1-R8 candidate had not yet been bound to one public release, installer, installed generation, and active-runtime receipt.
Prior Memory Wuxian incidents repeatedly distinguished packaged files, installed bytes, running effects, and foreground-safe Windows behavior.

failure_escalation.first_failure: Stop the failing stage, trace the shared canonical owner and all invariants it serves, and prefer correcting or deleting faulty internal logic over adding code.
failure_escalation.repair_review: Inspect the complete diff for additive bypasses, duplicated ownership, fallback branches, and seesaw risk before rerunning tests.
failure_escalation.after_limit: Do not publish. Preserve evidence and return for a new user decision.

exit_lifecycle.accepted: One frozen candidate passes full validation and independent evaluation.
exit_lifecycle.published: The exact accepted commit is tagged v2.19.0 with verified Windows, macOS, hash, and signed metadata assets.
exit_lifecycle.installed: The released Windows installer transaction commits on this device with the original archive root preserved.
exit_lifecycle.verified: The installed 2.19.0 collector, dashboard, shortcut, scheduler, and real capture effect are observed without foreground PowerShell or persisted-state regression.
exit_lifecycle.closed: Defect verification, workbook completion, promotion review, and precise platform status are recorded.
